ns2:group.ns2:title: 【硬件科普】想在电脑屏幕上看到正确的颜色，有多难？
ns2:group.ns2:description: 经常关注显示器的观众应该对色准这个参数并不陌生，它衡量的是显示器显示颜色的准确度。 衡量色准最常用的方法是国际照明委员会在2000年推出的CIE DE2000，简称ΔE。 这个数值越小，代表屏幕显示出的颜色和系统输出的颜色越接近，数值越大，则代表显示器显示的颜色与系统有偏差。 如果说亮度影响屏幕的可读性，色域决定画面的鲜艳程度，对比度影响画面的层次感，那色准就直接关系到屏幕显示的颜色是否准确真实。 那你知道ΔE到底是怎么测试出来的，ΔE一样的两台显示器观感是一样吗，ΔE多低才算好的显示器，买了ΔE足够低的显示器就能看到准确的颜色吗？

ns2:group.ns2:description:
CES Day 3 (and technically Day 4 for me) was packed with some of the most interesting and unexpected tech I’ve seen all week. From smart productivity gear and truly wireless TVs to AI glasses, robotics, and some absolutely random innovations, this was one of the most fun days to explore the show floor.
I kick things off with new products from Clicks, including the Power Keyboard, which combines a physical keyboard with wireless charging and multi-device support, plus the Clicks Communicator, a modern BlackBerry-inspired companion device focused on distraction-free messaging.
From there, we dive into Displace’s next-generation wireless TVs, including the Displace Pro 2 and the new Displace Hub, which can turn almost any existing TV into a clean, battery-powered, cable-free wall display — perfect for renters or anyone who hates drilling holes.
One of my favorite discoveries at CES came from Strada, showcased at ShowStoppers in partnership with OWC. Their approach to remote video editing lets you work directly with massive files stored on remote local drives without cloud uploads, proxies, or waiting, and honestly feels like a game-changer for video creators.
I also checked out a touchscreen add-on for MacBooks, AI-powered smart glasses, a surprisingly impressive ultra-short-throw projector, kid-friendly AirTag watches, MicroRGB TVs, wild robotics demos, and even a bike designed to keep you in a wheelie.

For months, reliable leaks suggested that Apple was preparing to launch new Apple TV 4K models and updated HomePod minis before the end of 2025. But now that we’re at the end of December, it’s clear that Apple isn’t releasing any new home hardware this year.
So what actually happened to the new Apple TV?
In this video, we break down why Apple likely delayed the next Apple TV 4K and what we now expect in early 2026 instead. Reports suggest Apple is sticking with the same familiar Apple TV design, but under the hood, the upgrades could be significant. Rumors point to Apple’s new N1 wireless chip with Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread support, along with a major performance jump from the A15 Bionic to a potential A17 Pro chip.
If that happens, the next Apple TV could support faster streaming, lower latency gaming, and possibly even Apple Intelligence features tied to the next generation of Siri on tvOS. There were also rumors of a built-in camera for FaceTime and gesture-based controls, though those features now seem far less likely.
We also cover what’s coming next for the HomePod mini. A second-generation HomePod mini is expected to arrive alongside the new Apple TV, featuring a newer S-series chip for better performance and responsiveness, possible Ultra Wideband upgrades, and new color options. However, recent leaks suggest Apple may rely on MediaTek wireless chips instead of its own N1 for lower-cost devices like HomePod mini.
With Apple’s smart home ecosystem expanding in 2026 and major Siri upgrades on the horizon, this delay may be part of a much bigger plan.
